A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AdaGC paper with all 28 pages, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content on pages 2–28; first-page differences concern correspondence information and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v3 reports original training experiments, downstream accuracies, spike scores, efficiency measurements and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain identical per-tensor EMA clipping, GlobalGC warm-up and optimizer integration procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same C4-en language-model pretraining, LAION-400M vision-language training and downstream benchmarks, including ImageNet. No dataset, task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including GlobalGC, ClipByValue, AGC, Clippy and ZClip, plus SPAM, Scaled Embed and WeSaR in Appendix E.2.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, precision, hyperparameters, evaluation metrics and zero-/two-shot procedures are identical in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter sweeps, initialization and warm-up ablations, adaptivity/locality comparisons and optimizer-state analyses remain unchanged in Sections 5.2 and 5.6 and Appendix F.

E5.justification: Seed-related descriptions and statistical reporting are identical. No repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, error bars or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings match. For example, Table 6 reports Llama-2 7B average zero-shot accuracy of 49.69% for GlobalGC and 51.01% for AdaGC in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations in Section 4 and the assumptions, lemmas, convergence theorems and proofs throughout Appendix G are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about gradient-centric stabilization, adaptive per-tensor clipping, optimizer compatibility, communication efficiency and empirical benefits.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability boundaries are unchanged, including Section 6 and Appendix A's limitations concerning cumulative numerical errors and silent infrastructure bugs.

D1.justification: Implementation guidance, Tables 9–10 hyperparameters, Appendix D's CLIP settings and the code-access link are unchanged. The additional general correspondence contact provides no new technical or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2, the comparison of clipping approaches in Table 2 and the reference list are identical; no cited work or research-positioning argument changes.

P1.justification: v4 adds existing coauthor Yanjun Ma and an email address to the first-page correspondence list alongside Dianhai Yu and Li Shen, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The paper's prose and section structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded correspondence footnote changes first-page line wrapping and spacing. All figures, tables, captions and remaining page layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 updates correspondence information and version metadata, with minor footnote reflow. The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, limitations and reproducibility information remain identical, establishing no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
